# R Script for Targeted NOAA SST Data Download

This script downloads NOAA OISST SST data for a specified
date range and geographic region from the thredds server. Datasets/noaa.oisst.v2.highres/sst.day.mean

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r libraries}

library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
library(glue)
library(fs)
library(httr2)     # For string manipulation
library(here)
library(ncdf4)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(cowplot)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r set directories}
# Set directories
project_dir <- here::here()

latlon <- read_csv(file.path(project_dir,"0_data","01_data_raw", "population_sites_IMOS.csv" ))
```


```{r}
# Download NOAA OISST v2.1 regional subsets using THREDDS NCSS
# Then calculate mean SST for each lat/lon bounding box

# -----------------------------
# 1. Inputs
# -----------------------------

years <- 1992:2025

nc_dir  <- "0_data/01_data_raw/oisst_subset_nc"
out_dir <- "0_data/01_data_raw/oisst_summary"


latlon <- latlon |>
  clean_names() |>
  rename(
    box_id  = population,  # change this if your ID column has another name
    lat_min = latmin,
    lat_max = latmax,
    lon_min = lonmin,
    lon_max = lonmax
  ) |>
  mutate(
    lat_min = as.numeric(lat_min),
    lat_max = as.numeric(lat_max),
    lon_min = as.numeric(lon_min),
    lon_max = as.numeric(lon_max)
  )

# -----------------------------
# 2. Convert longitude to OISST convention
# -----------------------------
# OISST uses 0–360 longitude, not -180–180.
# Eastern Australia longitudes are already positive, so this mostly matters
# if any longitudes are negative.

lon_to_360 <- function(x) {
  if_else(x < 0, x + 360, x)
}

latlon <- latlon |>
  mutate(
    lon_min_360 = lon_to_360(lon_min),
    lon_max_360 = lon_to_360(lon_max)
  )

# -----------------------------
# 3. Make one regional bounding box
# -----------------------------
# This downloads the smallest rectangle that contains all your boxes.
# Add a small buffer so edge grid cells are not missed.

buffer <- 0.25

regional_box <- latlon |>
  summarise(
    south = max(min(lat_min, na.rm = TRUE) - buffer, -89.875),
    north = min(max(lat_max, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer,  89.875),
    west  = max(min(lon_min_360, na.rm = TRUE) - buffer, 0.125),
    east  = min(max(lon_max_360, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer, 359.875)
  )

regional_box

# -----------------------------
# 4. Function to download one yearly regional subset
# -----------------------------

download_oisst_subset_month <- function(year, month, regional_box) {
  
  base_url <- glue(
    "https://www.psl.noaa.gov/thredds/ncss/grid/",
    "Datasets/noaa.oisst.v2.highres/sst.day.mean.{year}.nc"
  )
  
  start_date <- as.Date(glue("{year}-{str_pad(month, 2, pad = '0')}-01"))
  end_date   <- ceiling_date(start_date, "month") - days(1)
  
  dest <- file.path(
    nc_dir,
    glue("oisst_sst_subset_{year}_{str_pad(month, 2, pad = '0')}.nc")
  )
  
  if (file.exists(dest)) {
    message("Already downloaded: ", basename(dest))
    return(dest)
  }
  
  message("Downloading ", year, "-", str_pad(month, 2, pad = "0"))
  
  req <- request(base_url) |>
    req_url_query(
      var = "sst",
      north = regional_box$north,
      west  = regional_box$west,
      east  = regional_box$east,
      south = regional_box$south,
      horizStride = 1,
      time_start = glue("{start_date}T00:00:00Z"),
      time_end   = glue("{end_date}T00:00:00Z"),
      timeStride = 1,
      accept = "netcdf3"
    ) |>
    req_retry(
      max_tries = 5,
      backoff = ~ 10
    )
  
  # This prints the actual URL without performing the download
  # useful for debugging
  # req_dry_run(req)
  
  req_perform(req, path = dest)
  
  dest
}

download_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  year = years,
  month = 1:12)

# run the download function
nc_files <- pmap_chr(
  download_grid,
  \(year, month) {
    download_oisst_subset_month(
      year = year,
      month = month,
      regional_box = regional_box
    )
  }
)

#test plot temp across regional box
test <- rast(nc_files, subds = "sst")
test
plot(test[[1]])

# convert to correct lat and lons FUNCTION
read_oisst_fixed <- function(nc_file) {
  
  # read SST
  r <- rast(nc_file, subds = "sst")
  
  # read actual lon/lat coordinates from NetCDF
  nc <- ncdf4::nc_open(nc_file)
  on.exit(ncdf4::nc_close(nc))
  
  lon <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lon")
  lat <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc, "lat")
  
  dx <- median(diff(sort(unique(lon))))
  dy <- median(diff(sort(unique(lat))))
  
  # set extent using cell edges, not centres
  ext(r) <- ext(
    min(lon) - dx / 2,
    max(lon) + dx / 2,
    min(lat) - dy / 2,
    max(lat) + dy / 2
  )
  
  crs(r) <- "EPSG:4326"
  
  r
}

# convert to correct lat and lons
r <- read_oisst_fixed(nc_files[1])

ext(r)
res(r)
crs(r)

# create df
r_df <- as.data.frame(r[[1]], xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE)
names(r_df)[3] <- "sst"

latlon_plot <- latlon |>
  mutate(
    lat_lower = pmin(lat_min, lat_max),
    lat_upper = pmax(lat_min, lat_max),
    lon_lower = pmin(lon_min_360, lon_max_360),
    lon_upper = pmax(lon_min_360, lon_max_360))

# check convert worked
ggplot() +
  geom_raster(
    data = r_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = sst)) +
  geom_rect(
    data = latlon_plot,
    aes(
      xmin = lon_lower,
      xmax = lon_upper,
      ymin = lat_lower,
      ymax = lat_upper ),
    fill = NA,
    colour = "red",
    linewidth = 0.5) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "white") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
# -----------------------------
# 5. Extract mean SST per box
# -----------------------------

extract_box_sst <- function(nc_file, box_row) {
  
  message("Extracting ", box_row$box_id, " from ", basename(nc_file))
  
  sst <- read_oisst_fixed(nc_file)
  
  sst_crop <- crop(
    sst,
    ext(
      box_row$lon_min,
      box_row$lon_max,
      box_row$lat_min,
      box_row$lat_max
    )
  )
  
  sst_mean <- global(sst_crop, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)
  
  tibble(
    box_id = box_row$box_id,
    date = as.Date(time(sst_crop)),
    sst_mean = as.numeric(sst_mean[, 1])
  )
}

oisst_daily <- map_dfr(nc_files, function(nc_file) {
  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(latlon)), function(i) {
    extract_box_sst(nc_file, latlon[i, ])
  })
})

# -----------------------------
# 6. Summarise and save
# -----------------------------

oisst_daily <- oisst_daily |>
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date)) 

oisst_monthly <- oisst_daily |>
  group_by(box_id, year, month) |>
  summarise(
    sst_mean_monthly = mean(sst_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop" ) 

oisst_annual <- oisst_daily |>
  group_by(box_id, year) |>
  summarise(
    sst_mean_annual = mean(sst_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")
```

```{r basic temp plot for paper}
# create plotting dataset
oisst_plot <- oisst_annual |>

    population,

    names = c("latitude", "longitude"),

  mutate(
    latitude  = as.numeric(latitude),

pal <-c("#9B3441FF", "#D8443CFF","#DE597CFF","#E87B89FF","#E6A2A6FF","#FE9B00FF", "#F4C40FFF", "#FBE183FF", "#92C051FF",  "#2B9B81FF",  "#1F6E9CFF","#AA7AA1FF", "#9F5691FF", "#633372FF","#2B1B5A"  )

pl

  rename(population = box_id) |>

  summarise( sst_mean_monthly = mean(sst_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop" ) |> 
  mutate(
    population = factor(population, levels = unique(population)) )
```

```{r map of population locs}
latlon <- read_csv(file.path(project_dir,"0_data","01_data_raw", "population_sites_IMOS.csv" ))

# change population for map legend
latlon2 <- latlon |>
   separate_wider_delim(
    population,
    delim = "_",
    names = c("latitude", "longitude"),
    cols_remove = FALSE) |> 
  mutate(
    latitude  = as.numeric(latitude),
    longitude = as.numeric(longitude),
    population = paste(latitude, longitude, sep = ",")) |>
  arrange(desc(latitude)) |> 
  mutate(population = factor( population,levels = unique(population)))

# get polygons of each population
population_grid_sf <- latlon2 |>
  mutate(
    geometry = pmap(
      list(lonmin, lonmax, latmin, latmax),
      \(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) {
        st_polygon(list(
          matrix(
            c(
              xmin, ymin,
              xmax, ymin,
              xmax, ymax,
              xmin, ymax,
              xmin, ymin
            ),
            ncol = 2,
            byrow = TRUE
          )
        ))
      }
    )
  ) |>
  st_as_sf(crs = 4326)

# get land layers
# Australia land
aus <- rnaturalearth::ne_download(
  scale = 10,
  type = "land",
  category = "physical",
  returnclass = "sf") |>
  st_transform(4326)

# Crop to southeastern Australia / Tasmania
aus <- st_crop(
  aus,
  xmin = 135, xmax = 155,
  ymin = -45, ymax = -20)

# state boundaries
aus_states <- rnaturalearth::ne_states(
  country = "Australia",
  returnclass = "sf") |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  st_crop(
    xmin = 135, xmax = 155,
    ymin = -45, ymax = -20 )

pal <-c("#9B3441FF", "#D8443CFF","#DE597CFF","#E87B89FF","#E6A2A6FF","#FE9B00FF", "#F4C40FFF", "#FBE183FF", "#92C051FF",  "#2B9B81FF",  "#1F6E9CFF","#AA7AA1FF", "#9F5691FF", "#633372FF","#2B1B5A"  )

# map plot showing populations
p_population_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = population_grid_sf,
    aes(fill = population),
    colour = NA, alpha = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = aus, fill = "grey85", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = aus_states, fill = NA, colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_manual( values = pal,name = "Population") +
  coord_sf(
        xlim = c(143, 160),
        ylim =c(-45, -28),
        expand = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous( breaks = seq(-45.5, -10.5, by = 1),
                          labels = function(x) {
      ifelse(seq_along(x) %% 2 == 1, x, "")}) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(135.5, 160.5, by = 1),
                         labels = function(x) {
      ifelse(seq_along(x) %% 4 == 1, x, "")})+
  labs(
    x = expression("Longitude (" * degree * "E)"),
    y = expression("Latitude (" * degree * "S)")) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      keyheight = unit(0.5, "cm"),
      keywidth = unit(0.5, "cm") )) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.spacing.y = unit(0.1, "cm"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),)

p_population_map

# combine with temperature plot
pl <- pl+ theme_bw()+theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),)

map_plots <- pl+p_population_map
```
